38 The diagram shows a potentiometer and a fixed resistor connected across a 12 V battery of
negligible internal resistance.
fixed resistor
20 Ω
12 V
20 Ω
output
The fixed resistor and the potentiometer each have resistance 20 Ω. The circuit is designed to
provide a variable output voltage.
What is the range of output voltages?
A
0 – 6 V
B
0 – 12 V
C
6 – 12 V
D
12 – 20 V

hints: Notice the output is taken between the sliding contact and the bottom wire, so it is the voltage across only the part of the $20 \, \Omega$ potentiometer below the slider.
Connect this to the series circuit: the $20 \, \Omega$ fixed resistor and the full $20 \, \Omega$ potentiometer share the $12 \, \text{V}$ supply, so find the voltage at the top of the potentiometer.
Compare the two slider extremes: slider at the bottom wire includes zero resistance, slider at the junction with the fixed resistor includes the full potentiometer voltage.
walkthrough: Identify the circuit as a series potential divider: $20 \, \Omega$ fixed resistor on top and $20 \, \Omega$ potentiometer below, across $12 \, \text{V}$.
Total resistance is $R = 20 + 20 = 40 \, \Omega$, so the series current is $I = V/R = 12/40 = 0.30 \, \text{A}$.
Voltage across the whole potentiometer is $V_p = I \times 20 = 0.30 \times 20 = 6.0 \, \text{V}$, so the top of the potentiometer is $6.0 \, \text{V}$ above the bottom wire.
With the slider at the bottom, the output includes $0 \, \Omega$ and $V_{out} = 0 \, \text{V}$.
With the slider at the top of the potentiometer, the output includes the full $20 \, \Omega$ and $V_{out} = 6.0 \, \text{V}$.
The variable range is therefore $0-6 \, \text{V}$. This is option A.

A.explanation: The slider can select $0 \, \Omega$ to $20 \, \Omega$ of the lower potentiometer, giving $0 \, \text{V}$ to the full $6 \, \text{V}$ across the potentiometer.

B.explanation: The full $12 \, \text{V}$ cannot appear at the output because the $20 \, \Omega$ fixed resistor always drops part of the battery e.m.f.

C.explanation: The output is measured from the bottom wire, so moving the slider to the bottom gives $0 \, \text{V}$, not $6 \, \text{V}$.

D.explanation: Voltages above the $12 \, \text{V}$ supply are impossible in this passive divider with negligible internal resistance.
